MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 14, 2021
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Kelley at
5:04 p.m., on September 14, 2021, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on September 9, 2021, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted
at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Raths
  Council Member Sachs
  Mayor Pro Tem Member Bucknum
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Real Property Negotiators: Stein Mart Property 25282 Marguerite
  Parkway; Agency Negotiators: Dennis Wilberg, Keith Rattay, Elaine Lister, Cheryl
  Dyas and William Curley. Negotiating Party: Kinstler Family Trust. Under
  Negotiation-Price and Terms

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:05p.m., Mayor Kelley recessed the meeting to Closed Session. The City Council
reconvened at 6:01 p.m. with five City Council Members present.

City Council Minutes  1  September 14, 2021
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley stated that the City Council was given one final overview and confirmation
of the Purchase and Sale Agreement which will be addressed under 19C. No reportable action
occurred in closed session in regards to that document.

INVOCATION: Council Member Sachs

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Kelley

PRESENTATIONS

P1. School Spotlight - Castille Elementary School

  Received presentation by Principal Nelson.

P2. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Kelley presented certificates of commendation to "Marines of the Quarter" Corporal
  Justin Hamlett and Corporal Jonathan Moore, and "Noncommissioned Officers of the
  Quarter" Corporal R.M. Schartner and Sergeant Sarah Payne.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sharon Campbell, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the Core Vision plan and feels it is a very positive step
forward for our community.

Larry Garner, M.V.: Announced that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee held their first Fourth
of July Home Decorating Contest this past July and will now have the first Halloween Home
Decorating Contest.

Steve Bell, San Clemente: Thanked the City Council and the many volunteers for their support
during Relay for Life. The event raised $119,000.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Read two letters from the former Secretary of State Alex Padilla to the City
regarding cumulative voting stating that his office did not agree to draft or sponsor any legislation.

Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Questioned the City Attorney report on the acquisition of the Stein Mart
Property and asked when the residents approved this plan. He stated that this plan was never
presented to the residents like City Hall went to the voters for approval and voiced his concern on
he cost.

Walt Lawson, M.V.: Addressed his concerns on terms of Council Members and asked that all five
City Council seats are up in 2022. Complained that the time line on District Hearings should be
moved up due to the Holidays.

Rudy Padrol, M.V.: Announced that there will be a Susan G. Komen Walk around Lake Mission
Viejo on September 25 and encourage residents to attend.
City Council Minutes  2  September 14, 2021
 Robert Breton, M.V.: Addressed the City Council regarding the exhibit at the Mission Viejo
Library on the Japanese Concentration Camps called “The Reach of Civil Liberties” and he
encourages residents to visit the exhibit that will be on display until September 30.

Written comment received from Alex Berk, M.V., asking that the City Council consider
transitioning to Community Choice Energy.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Items 14 was removed from the Consent Calendar for separate consideration.

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
remainder of the Consent Calendar as outlined below. On roll call, said motion carried by the
following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT: None

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 24, 2021, as presented.

2.  Check Register Dated August 13, 2021 in the Amount of $4,682,241.91

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Check Register Dated August 20, 2021 in the Amount of $436,488.92

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  FY 2021/22 Investment Policies

  Adopted Resolution 21-32 Approving the City's Investment Policy for FY 2021/22, CDFA
  Resolution 21-02 Approving the Authority's Investment Policy for FY 2021/22, and Housing
  Authority Resolution 21-02 Approving the Mission Viejo Housing Authority Investment
  Policy for FY 2021/22.

5.  Investment Management Services

  Approved the second amendment to contract for investment management services with
  Chandler Asset Management for a two-year period October 1, 2021 through September 30,
  2023 in the amount of $50,000.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2021

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  September 14, 2021
 7.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for July 2021

  Received and filed.

8.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for July 2021

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2021

  Received and filed.

10. City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2020/21

  Received and filed the accompanying City Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2020/21.

11. Community Development Financing Authority (CDFA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for
  Fiscal Year 2020/21

  Received and filed the accompanying CDFA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2020/21.

12. Professional Services Agreement Between the City of Mission Viejo, the Mission Viejo
  Housing Authority, and Stradling, Yocca, Carlson & Rauth for Special Counsel Legal
  Services

  Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Stradling, Yocca, Carlson & Rauth
  (A21-45) for Special Counsel.

13. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA)Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2020/21

  Received and filed the accompanying MVHA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2020/21.

15. 800 MHz Countywide Coordinated Communication System

  Authorized the City Manager to Approve the Joint Agreement for the 800 MHz Countywide
  Communication System.

16. Correction to City of Mission Viejo Annual Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year
  Capital Improvement Program

  Adopted a corrected City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M (M2) Seven-Year Capital
  Improvement Program, beginning with the 2021/2022 fiscal year.

17. Jeronimo Road and Marguerite Parkway Intersection Improvements (CIP 21246)

City Council Minutes  4  September 14, 2021
   (1) Approved Construction Contract Change Order to GMC Engineering, Inc. in the amount
  of $59,218 for additional work; (2) certified the completion of and accept the improvements
  for the subject project; (3) authorized the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (4)
  authorized the City Clerk to record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and
  to release the faithful performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively,
  after the date of recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens
  being filed with the City; and (5) authorized the release of the final retention 35 days after the
  date of recordation of the Notice of Completion.

18. First Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and Processing
  Agreement

  (1) Approved the First Amendment to the Mission Viejo Library Materials Purchasing and
  Processing Agreement with Ingram Library Services, LLC, through June 30, 2023 in an
  amount not to exceed $400,000 pending approval of the FY 22-23 budget; and (2) authorized
  issuance of a purchase order to Ingram Library Services, LLC for the period of July 1, 2021
  through June 30, 2022, in an amount not to exceed $200,000.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

14. Amendment to the City of Mission Viejo Values Statement

  Motion made by Council Member Goodell, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, to delay
  the approval of this item until the next strategic planning process.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

OLD BUSINESS

19. CORE AREA VISION PLAN IMPLEMENTATION

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg gave a brief overview.

  A. Review of Core Area Vision Plan

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay
  gave the presentation.

  B. Funding Options Discussion for Core Area Vision Plan Implementation

  Director of Administrative Services Cheryl Dyas and Fieldman, Rolapp &Associates,
  Financial Consultant Jim Fabian presented the report.

  C. Purchase and Sale Agreement with Kinstler Family Trust

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the report.
City Council Minutes  5  September 14, 2021
   D. Collaborative Design Team for Core Area Vision Plan Implementation

  Assistant City Manager Keith Rattay presented the report.

  Jessica Fritz, M.V.: Voiced concerns with the subsidy cuts for the purchase of this
  development come on the back of you families. She urged the Council to consider what this
  will cost going forward.

  Larry Gilbert, M.V.: Asked for the name of the appraisers on this project and would like to
  see a copy of the appraisal and will be submitting a records request. He asked if the Director
  of Administrative Services can provide him with the city’s current debt service prior to this
  project.
  He stated that this should go to the voters to approve.

  Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Asked the Council where was the desire of the public to purchase a
  store front building for $43 million debt. She stated that the Council’s political careers will
  be over if this purchase goes forward. She feels the Stein Mart building is way overpriced.
  Asked that the appraisal be made public and that the CC&R’s for this shopping center are
  important.

  Eric Cernick, Newport Beach: Commented that the CC&R’s state that the City can not do
  their Vision Plan. He stated he is going to defend the CC&R’s.

  Cathy Allen, M.V.: Voiced her approval of the project. She stated this will revitalize our
  community.

  Ken Hira, Coto de Caza: Commented on land uses and everything is changing and that
  thinking out of the box is a positive thing. He is in favor of this project.

  Alan Dibartolomeo, Irvine: Complimented the City on the improvements made at the Oso
  Creek Golf Course. Stated that the City’s Master Plan will create a great gathering place for
  residents and will benefit the community and the City.

  Jeff Creer, M.V.: Stated he is thrilled about this project and he has been a resident for twenty
  years. He feels this will be a crown jewel of our community and he hopes that property owners
  will soften their hearts and be supportive of this project.

  Jennifer Ward, Los Alamitos: Introduced herself as the Senior Vice President in Advocacy
  in Government Relations for the Orange County Business Council (OCBC). She stated that
  the OCBC supports this Vision Plan.

  Anthony Elia, M.V.: Suggested the reuse of Stein Mart and Michaels retail store be used as
  union sponsored technical schools for future journeyman plumbers, electricians, heating and
  air conditioning technicians, and finish carpenters. He is not in favor of this project.

  Martha Uriarte, M.V.: Questioned that she never received a formal survey on this project and
  she is not in favor of it and asked where the transparency was to the residents.

City Council Minutes  6  September 14, 2021
   Doug Zielasko, M.V.: Stated that the vision of the Chamber of Commerce is to promote the
  economic well being of businesses within the city limits. The Core Vision Plan is clearly
  aligned with our goals and objectives and they are truly enthusiastic about prospects of what
  the Core Vision Plan will offer to small business growth and excited what this project will
  bring to the community as a catalyst of unity and spirit. He thanked the City Council and
  asked to let the Chamber know how they can support in any way.

  Charlie Kinstler, Laguna Beach: Stated that he owns four parcels in the Mission Viejo Village
  Center. He was at the original Core Vision Plan Meeting in 2017 and expressed that there
  were a lot of ideas and excitement. Expressed that the presentation tonight is exactly what the
  center needs and looks forward to the next steps in watching the Core Vision Plan.

  Robert Breton, M.V.: Highlighted that the Core Vision Plan is a step in the right direction. He
  feels this center has always had the potential to be something greater.

  Kris Yellin, M.V.: Spoke in favor of the project and stated that our City behind other cities.
  She expressed that the center is dilapidated and is an embarrassment. Voiced concerns of the
  reduction of subsidies that the residents view as community programs. She stated parking
  may be a concern.

  Mindy Gellar, M.V.: Announced she is one of the owners of The Patio across the street and
  stated she has not had one vacancy for years. She stated that she has never once been
  contacted by the City regarding the shopping center. Voiced her concerns.

  Vince Stemen, M.V.: Stated that he has never heard about this project and stated that this
  project can’t be compared to the San Antonio River Walk. Encouraged that the City Council
  should vote no to borrow more time to get the residents more involved.

  Bob Ruesch, M.V.: He stated he is in favor of this project and to understand that change is
  inevitable but growth is optional. Mission Viejo continues to change and the reality is that
  the City is looking a little worn out and encouraged the City Council To move forward with
  this project.

  Wade Weiman, M.V.: Complained that he never received any notice about this meeting. He
  asked that in the future that the business owners need to be notified. Expressed concerns
  about the parking and asked various questions.

  Written comments were received in favor of the project from the following: Barbara Thomas
  from the South Orange County Economic Coalition.

  Written comments were received in opposition of the project from the following: Rachel
  Christine Holland, M.V., Terrill Holland, M.V., Rosalie De Vito, Carleene Hyde, M.V., Paul
  Vinnicof, M.V., Rose Tingle, M.V., Dennis Ramsey, M.V., and Sharon and Ralph Smith,
  M.V.

  Deputy General Manager Don Bunts of Santa Margarita Water District briefly discussed the
  role that the Water District has in this project.

City Council Minutes  7  September 14, 2021
   Council Members asked various questions of staff.

  City Manager Dennis Wilberg addressed the statements made this evening regarding that the
  business owners were not notified of this project. He read an excerpt from an email from one
  of the business owners to the City “We have decided to only have the owners meeting on
  Thursday July 22. Once this takes place we can discuss having the City attend a future
  meeting”. City Manager Wilberg said despite our request we were not included in the
  meetings they decided to have. The City Manager also explained that the City has an
  electronic newsletter that goes out to over 30,000 subscribers weekly, and a presence on every
  social media platform. He said the City attempted and asked to be invited to an owners
  meeting but the City was told no.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1) adopt
  City Council Resolution 21-33 Directing the City Manager to Take Actions Necessary to
  Finance the Core Area Vision Plan Project; (2) adopt Community Development Financing
  Authority Resolution 21-03 Declaring its Official Intent to Reimburse Expenditures From
  Proceeds of a Future Issue of Tax-Exempt Lease Revenue Bonds; (3) authorize execution of
  agreement (A21-47) by Mayor Kelley; (4) award a contract to Labco (A21-48) in an amount
  not to exceed $78,000.00; (5) award a contract to RDC-S111, Inc. dba Studio One Eleven
  (A21-49) in an amount not to exceed $74,300.00; (6) issue a Purchase Order to RJM Design
  Group, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $92,700.00; and (7) issue a Purchase Order to Johnson-
  Frank & Associates, Inc. in an amount not to exceed $ 49,087.50.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

20. Transportation Corridor Agency (TCA) Report

  Received report from Mayor Kelley.

CITY MANAGER REPORT

 21. 2021 Interactive Annual Walk Against Drugs Funding Request

  Deputy Nawar Alkawadri and Community Services Officer Nick Rickers gave the report
  presentation.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Sachs, to approve
  funding in an amount not to Exceed $20,000 for students and schools participating in the 2021
  Interactive Walk Against Drugs Event.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
City Council Minutes  8  September 14, 2021
   NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CITY ATTORNEY/CITY CLERK REPORT

22. Update on District Voting

  Received update from City Attorney Bill Curley and City Clerk Kimberly Schmitt.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

23. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell had no further comments.

Council Member Raths

Announced that he visited the Moulton Niguel Water District headquarters. Stated that he attended
the service at the Aliso Viejo Town Center for Staff Sergeant Hoover who was one of the thirteen
Marines killed in Afghanistan. Lastly, he thanked Aliso Viejo for hosting this service.

Council Member Sachs

Council Member Sachs had no further comments.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum thanked the audience that stayed to the end of this Meeting. Gave a
shout out to Stephen Hines who his looking for ways to volunteer in our community. She also
thanked Larry Garner ad Misty Webb from the Mission Viejo Activities Community for sharing
upcoming events. Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum also thanked Sharon Campbell for attending this
evening and speaking in favor of the Core Vision Plan. She stressed that the City wants to work
with the business and property owners in the Village Center and looks forward to the next steps to
make a positive difference.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley gave a shout out for the Relay 4 Life and Steve Bell and all his hard work for the last
twenty years. She attended the Wall of Recognition Ceremony honoring Pam Smith and Elizabeth
Busick. Finally, she commended Chief Vuong, Community Services Officer Rickers, Deputy
Madrigal and the Explorers for putting together in a short time a Patriot Day Event on September
11. Mayor Kelley gave a shout out to Deputy Olivia Coco who sang the National Anthem.

City Council Minutes  9  September 14, 2021
 Commended the speeches by Council Member Raths, Orange County Fire Authority Chief
Downing, and Deputy Murphy who represented law enforcement.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 10:27 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Mike Waugh and Investment Advisory
Commissioner Richard Steinhoff to Tuesday, September 28, 2021, at 5:00 p.m.

.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 28, 2021

City Council Minutes  10  September 14, 2021
